description: Applies the FSharp.Refactor analyzers' quick fixes to F# code from the command line. Point it at a project, a script, a solution, a directory or a glob; --dry-run reports without editing. The tool clarifies the (agent-generated or old) code's intent, reduces non-alphanumeric noise, and uses built-in .NET libraries more efficiently.
releaseNotes:
0.8.27: Seven correctness rules, the F# twins of CSharp.Refactor's CR0160-CR0171 family where F# does not rule the hazard out by design. FR0159: `float (sum / count)` divides as integers before it widens - the editor offers `float sum / float count`, a sweep never applies it, and a literal operand or a product dividend (`float (screenW / 2)`, `float (x * mw / tw)`: a pixel centre, a scaled coordinate) is the editor's alone unless `{ "FR0159": { "all": true } }`. FR0160: a handler raising a new exception without the one it caught gains it as the constructor's trailing argument where the type has that constructor (`raise (X("m", ex))`, a `_`/`:? T` pattern gaining `as ex`); `failwith` in a handler that never reads what it caught is a note. FR0161: a mutating method on the struct a property returns mutates a copy - the one such copy F# does not refuse at compile time. FR0162: check-then-assign on a module-level or `static let` mutable races; `lazy` runs the factory once. FR0163: a `System.Threading.Timer` nothing references is collected mid-flight (a `System.Timers.Timer` is not - measured). FR0164: a collection edited inside a `for` over itself throws at the next step; the loop walks `Array.ofSeq items`. FR0165: a local `DateTime` compared with or subtracted from a UTC one flips with the timezone. Three rules widen: FR0055 notes the narrow catch that is TryParse as control flow (`with :? FormatException -> 0`) and offers the rewrite where the catch covers what TryParse turns into false; FR0118 notes an awaiting loop under a token that never observes it; FR0123 notes `SemaphoreSlim.Wait`/`ReaderWriterLockSlim.Enter*Lock`/`Mutex.WaitOne` with no `finally` release and, where the release is a statement of the same block, moves the statements between under a `try` and the release into its `finally`. Every gate the C# side learned on real repositories came along - a mutation in a lambda is deferred, a store under `lock gate <| fun () ->` is guarded, an `IList<_>` may be concurrent, a compound emptiness test is a reconnecting holder, not a lazy - and a dry run over fourteen projects of the corpus proposed no fix and no false note. The property suite now typechecks what it generates: eleven rule families of shapes over a two-file script (a stub declares the test-framework and logger namespaces some rules gate on), four properties over every family at once, a per-shape check that each shape reaches its rule - or, for a shape spelled `!FR0162`, that the rule stays quiet on it, the false-positive guard a real repository taught - and a catalog test that every rule has a shape or a stated reason none can. It found three defects: FR0065's whole-setting comment-out put the comment before the `()` and moved the block's offside column, FR0080 read a string literal inside a block comment as code where the compiler stays in the comment, and the shared test-file marker did not know `[<TestCaseSource>]`. FR0012 no longer withholds the `isNull` hint beside a boolean operator: the named-argument guard took every parent application for a call, `||` included, so `x = null || flag` was never rewritten while `if x = null` was; an operator application is not a call, and the replacement stands bare there (`isNull x || flag`). The Visual Studio extension's tagger constructs `FrTagger` with `new`, as FS0760 asks.
 0.8.26: A property-based suite, `tests/FSharp.Refactor.PropertyTests`, joins the example-based one: FsCheck generates a module of declarations shaped for the parse-only rules, and boolean terms over three integers with an interpreter as the oracle, and the properties are the invariants the rules promise - a parse-only fix keeps the file parseable, no rule throws on a tree the parser recovered from damaged text, applying edits one at a time reaches a fixed point, and the boolean rewrites (FR0108/FR0109, the negation and De Morgan hints, FR0010, FR0013) keep the function's truth table at every step. It found one defect, shared by every rule that replaces a bracketed expression with a bare one: a replacement that begins or ends in an identifier character, put where the brackets were, runs into the token beside it - `match not (a <> b)with` is legal F#, and the hint's `a = b` left `bwith`. FR0012, FR0013, FR0094, FR0097, FR0098, FR0108 and FR0109 now put one space on the side that would glue, and none anywhere else. The FR0012 purity probe reads an interpolated string part by its case rather than a catch-all, so a part the parser adds later cannot pass as literal text.
 0.8.25: Every help link names the rule's own section of Rules.md: the SARIF rule metadata and the HTML report link to `Rules.md#fr0103--idiom`, the anchor GitHub gives the `### FR0103 — idiom` heading, where a bare `#fr0103` lands on nothing; a test slugs every heading the way GitHub does and holds the catalog's anchors against them. The Visual Studio extension's package lists a content type for every part again: manifest.json and catalog.json were written after the payload was enumerated, and a part without one made the whole file "not a valid VSIX package" once the FSAC payload's own .json files no longer hid it.
 0.8.24: The apply tool's build-configuration probe reads each compile item by the path the project spells. The item set is keyed by lowercased paths for membership, and the probe read the file through the key: on a case-sensitive file system `library.fs` is not `Library.fs`, an unreadable file counts as branching on the configuration, and on Linux every project got the extra Release pass and the extra Release build (the CI's consumer-verification test failed on the wording of a build it did not expect). The probe now reads the spelled path, and a test writes a project whose item's case the file system has to match. The wait on a child build no longer has the run at its mercy: after a `dotnet build` exits, the wait for its output pipes to close gets ten seconds, not forever, and the child runs with MSBuild node reuse off, since a worker node kept for the next build inherits the pipes and held the run - and the test host - for as long as it lived.
 0.8.23: A code audit of the whole source and of everything since 0.8.12, each finding reproduced through the rule before being fixed. Rewrites that compiled and silently changed behaviour now stand down. FR0157 keeps a match with a guarded catch-all (`| v when v.Length = 4 ->` above `| "POST" ->` was deleted as dead), a `| null ->` arm, or a variable pattern two module-level constants spell, and resolves a constant by its declaration rather than its name (a nested module's `let kind = "dir"` was read as the file's `let kind = "file"`). FR0156 refuses a loop whose other statements are not unit (a discarded `d.TryAdd(x, x)` had become a second yield), a delegate element type (Add converted the lambda where a yield does not) and a Span read in the moved region; FR0158 asks the typed tree the same Span question and stands down without one. FR0071 hoists only arithmetic, comparison and boolean operators over values no call in the loop can change (`let line = reader |> readLine` had left the loop reading one line forever). FR0050 spells `sum`/`sumBy` for a floating accumulator only, since FSharp.Core's sum is checked where the loop wrapped; an integer accumulation gets the `fold`. FR0107 requires a predicate of FSharp.Core and string members only, so a logging `validate f` runs as often as before. FR0004 keeps the eager copy in front of a lambda that mutates a collection or names the source (`rs |> Seq.toList |> List.iter (fun x -> rs.Remove x |> ignore)` threw once it enumerated `rs` itself). FR0003 composes only stages whose arguments are literals or immutable values (`addN (compute())` had run once instead of per element). FR0044 turns into `reraise ()` only a binder of the whole exception, never a case field (`ParseFailed(_, inner) -> raise inner` had rethrown the wrapper). FR0118 leaves the calls of a `with` handler or `finally` alone, where a cancelled operation must still roll back. FR0075 treats a task the disposable produced and handed to any call as in flight (`tasks.Add(client.GetStringAsync u)` then `Task.WhenAll` disposed the client under its requests). FR0015 spells the ordinal `StartsWith` overload and keeps a regex ending in `$`, which matches before a final newline. FR0039 keeps OrdinalIgnoreCase as the fix for every lowering (the current-culture `ToLower()` differs from it on the Turkish dotless i alone, and the idiomatic spelling is taken over a CurrentCultureIgnoreCase nobody writes), and a lowered call that already names a StringComparison keeps the author's choice: `x.ToLower().StartsWith("a", StringComparison.Ordinal)` becomes `x.StartsWith("a", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`, where the tuple argument had stood the rule down. Guards that had closed too much reopened to their precise condition: FR0107 follows a same-file predicate into its body and rewrites when nothing there has an effect, standing down only for a callee it cannot read; FR0071 hoists `/` and `%` over a non-zero literal divisor again and vetoes a read of a mutable only when a function the loop calls (same file, followed three deep) assigns it - a local `let mutable` included, since a closure has captured one as a ref cell since F# 4.0 - scanning everything between the insertion point and the loop, the pipeline head included, and treating a function-typed field, a property getter or an active pattern as a callee it cannot follow; FR0157 deletes an unguarded `| null ->` arm as the dead arm the proof shows it to be, though never one that shares an or-pattern with a literal; a built-in FR0012 hint without a typed tree stands down inside a computation-expression body only, where a custom operation can live, and fires everywhere else as before; FR0075 treats a CancellationTokenSource whose token reaches anything but an awaited BCL call - a user call, Async.Start, a constructor, a record field, a property set, a collection - as in flight; FR0029 keeps a `let` whose right side can throw (a property read such as `opt.Value` or `t.Result` counts; a record field or a plain value does not) inside the task when the task can leave the file through a public or interface member - written in one, or in a private or class binding a public member hands out - whose callers may rely on a faulted Task (SQLProvider's ISqlProvider.ExecuteSprocCommandAsync), and still hoists it from bindings that stay private. The apply tool judges a verification build "not verified" only when it stopped at the time cap (a marker on the stopped process's line, not prose), so a pre-existing MSB3073 or NU5xxx failure identical with and without the fixes keeps them as before; an abandoned typecheck is cancelled rather than left running; and a csproj or vbproj in the same solution that references the project is built as part of verification, its compiler errors weighed like the F# build's (FSharp.Azure.Quantum's C# builder cast to a union case class the run had made a struct, and the F# build alone saw success), or, where it does not build here, holds the project's public surface in place. The apply tool reads a project file's text with its XML comments removed wherever it matches the text rather than evaluating it: welendus's WelendusLogic.fsproj keeps `<!-- <TargetFrameworks>netstandard2.0;net48</TargetFrameworks> -->` above the live element, the first match was the commented one, and every run asked MSBuild for a net48 pass that no restore had produced (NETSDK1005) - the same read now guards the DefineConstants and ProjectReference matches, so a reference an author commented away no longer makes a referencer. FR0110 spells the raising arm it adds inside a computation expression with the siblings' `return` (or `yield`): a bare `raise` arm there is a unit-typed statement, and welendus's `match!` in a task had the fix rolled back on TaskCode<_, unit> against TaskCode<_, T>. FR0055 offers its IO-only narrowing of a catch-all only when the typed tree agrees that every call on the line is System.IO's (or FSharp.Core's): `Some (Path.GetFileName d, Checkpoint.loadMetadata p)` was narrowed on the strength of the `Path`, and the user function's JsonException escaped a command meant to skip junk directories (Fuuga); the assembly-loading and font-lookup probes put back by hand in SQLProvider and Kasino were the same shape. FR0142 leaves a test whose last expression is a value (NUnit's ExpectedResult was no longer compared). FR0002 keeps a match whose arm calls the enclosing `let rec` (a tail call inside `Option.map` is none). The map-fusion hints (`List.map f (List.map g x) ===> List.map (g >> f) x` and the Array and Seq twins, FSharpLint's defaults) fuse only two mappers whose calls are provably effect-free - FSharp.Core functions, union cases, and lambdas that call nothing but FSharp.Core and System.String and hold no statement, assignment, loop or printf - since the fused form interleaves calls the two sweeps ran one after the other; and a built-in hint stands down where the typed tree is not clean, so a file with an error, or a --parse-only run, no longer loses a computation expression's custom operation to `id x ===> x`. Three rewrites that did not compile: FR0049's taskify puts `return` before a parenthesised tail rather than inside it, FR0013 keeps the parentheses of an application that is itself indexed or applied (`List.sort(xs)[0]`), and `Text.patNames` reads record, cons, optional and named-field patterns, so FR0095 no longer takes an `id` a pattern bound for FSharp.Core's; FR0147 checks the bare names of patterns against an open it adds, and FR0155 treats a flexible `#Node` use as a veto. The shared byref-like guard recorded nothing for a whole file once a `ReadOnlySpan` indexer threw on its declaration location, disarming the guard for seven rules; each use now keeps its own answer. The apply tool: a rule that throws is reported and skipped, not the run ended, and counted in the exit code; a verification build that ran into its time cap, or failed without one compiler error, puts the fixes back as unverified instead of keeping them as pre-existing breakage; a typecheck abandoned after a pass wrote its files writes them back first, and the abandonment now returns at the cap (FSharp.Core's RunSynchronously waited for the check to finish regardless); the framework flags reset on every path out of the framework loop; a checkout's private SDK leaves DOTNET_ROOT and PATH when the next checkout has none; one unreadable directory no longer empties the script call-site probe. Configuration: `"Hints": false` at the root disables FR0012 as the documentation says, and the strings "true"/"false"/"on"/"off" count as booleans. The Visual Studio extension no longer writes to a sidecar that has exited (which took Visual Studio down from a timer thread), pins a fix's edits to the snapshot they were computed against and skips them when that text has moved, and keeps a failing fetch or edit off the UI thread's exception path.
 0.8.22: FR0157's serializer guard reads the VALUE handed to a reflective head, not only a type argument: a record, or a collection of one, passed or piped to `JsonSerializer.Serialize`, behind a field or property (`Serialize wrapper.Items`) or anywhere along a curried call (`Serialize options value`), stands the rule down, since every field of it is read by reflection and a union field would serialize differently. The union a run adds carries the widest visibility of the slots it types - private when they are all private, internal when one is internal or the component spans files, public only when a public one is among them - so a run without --api-changes never adds a public type to a library by itself. Two audit tests that assumed Windows path semantics now pass on Linux too.


 Earlier versions: CHANGELOG.md in the repository (https://github.com/Thorium/fsharp-refactor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
